reviewer_mode: independent hostile AAA mythic-force and composite pre-Unity gate

scope.isolated_question: Whether the accepted Round009 sheet preserves identity, engineering, one-weapon continuity, and two-hand contact while replacing industrial-technician presentation with a singular ownable mythic storm-warden silhouette expressed through convincing full-body combat force.
claims_not_made: 3D, rig, mesh, UV, deformation, collision, animation, LOD, engine, or production readiness
legal originality, exclusivity, copyright clearance, or trademark clearance

round009_candidates.fresh_finding: Identity and one connected weapon survive, but the low hand line, centered torso, and presentation stance do not express full-body force.
Layering and asymmetry improve, but the hands remain below the body power center and the shoulders do not convincingly carry blade load.
The raised grip and wide base improve readiness, but the ring-like guard changes the accepted weapon language and introduces a familiar historical-sword cue.

This is the strongest Round009 frame: it restores a low rectangular guard, retains one complete weapon and separated two-hand contact, and adds substantial costume layering. The wide grounded pose remains a controlled studio guard rather than a decisive force event.

isolated_decision.finding: The accepted sheet retains the core person, handed equipment path, heavy-right-leg asymmetry, complete weapon, and auditable same-hilt grip, while replacing much of the workwear read with denser layered protection. It still fails the complete isolated target because the tasset-and-odachi language remains familiar and the broad studio guard pose lacks a decisive whole-body load, impact, acceleration, or recovery chain.

private_benchmark_comparison.method: Six relevant full-body combat and costume-authoring references were selected from a private visual inventory, randomly reordered, and placed in unlabeled two-panel sheets with independently randomized candidate side, aspect-preserving fit, neutral padding, and no retouching. Judgment was blind to side; all extraction and comparison files were destroyed after inspection.

comparisons.focus: weapon acceleration and torso-to-arm force chain
comparisons.finding: The candidate is clearer as a costume sheet, but its shoulders, hips, and blade remain held rather than accelerating through a committed combat action.
The candidate's complete pale-ground figure, split shoulder device, counter-diagonal blade, and heavy grounding leg produce the more immediate full-body read.

comparisons.focus: action arc, threat response, and authored motion
comparisons.finding: The benchmark communicates direction, timing, and risk through the whole figure; the candidate remains a posed readiness display.
Candidate straps, plates, and conductor are coherent, but they do not visibly react to a comparable impact or directional load.

comparisons.focus: weapon mass and overhead load commitment
comparisons.finding: The candidate's long blade is plausible in outline, but the body does not sell its mass through spinal, shoulder, elbow, and foot loading.

comparisons.focus: layered costume hierarchy and authored material separation
comparisons.finding: The candidate presents a strong readable hierarchy of cloth, ceramic, blackened metal, and copper across the entire figure.

categories.finding: The face, braid, shoulder device, diagonal conductor, hip module, and heavy-right-leg identity survive, though Round009 is one posed view and small construction details drift from the turnaround.
The accepted Round007 four-view sheet remains clean and useful for modeling, with only modest construction and orthographic drift.
Proportions and support are credible, but the broad stance reads arranged; shoulder, pelvis, spine, and feet do not form a fully convincing high-force kinetic chain.
The mature lived-in face and asymmetric braid remain recognizable, while eye shape, brow treatment, and facial plane emphasis still vary across sheets.
Round009 adds substantial cloth, ceramic, metal, and copper layering with strong value and surface separation, though some plate repetition feels generated rather than structurally resolved.
The yoke, long blade, tassets, and giant grounding greave read clearly, but the overall role remains too close to a familiar armored odachi fighter to be singular at an AAA character-brand bar.
Both closed hands occupy separated regions of one continuous wrapped hilt, with visible ingress, egress, pressure, and credible wrist alignment.
The complete odachi, low guard, base cage, long hilt, blade, pommel, and tip are coherent; balance, cage fastening, and body response to the blade's mass remain underexplained.
Civilian, fetish, and glossy-plastic reads are reduced, but layered hanging tassets, the curved odachi, and the guard pose retain conspicuous generic samurai-adjacent coding.

The sheet is polished concept art with stronger costume authorship, but only 2 of 6 blind comparisons meet the bar; action specificity, physical force, and ownable role language remain below benchmark.

composite_decision.finding: Round009 repairs much of the industrial-costume ceiling without losing the solved grip or weapon continuity, but the complete pack fails the isolated target, total score, category floor, and blinded benchmark gates.

single_biggest_remaining_visual_gap: A singular mechanics-driven storm-warden combat silhouette: the current samurai-adjacent tassets, odachi language, and wide studio guard must become one unmistakably ownable full-body force event in which blade mass visibly drives the spine, shoulders, pelvis, feet, and layered equipment.

pre_unity_state.unityUnlockCondition: paid 3D generation authorized by a passing fresh composite gate
